children: Gulf Egypt Hotels & Tourism, a subsidiary of Kuwait's United Real Estate Company (URC), has launched a 31,780-square-metre (sqm) mixed-use development in Heliopolis, Cairo, following the signing of a protocol agreement with Egypt's Armed Forces Engineering Authority.
The project, located on Al Orouba Road, will comprise residential, commercial, administrative, hospitality and entertainment components within an integrated master plan, the company said.
Gulf Egypt is currently carrying out technical and economic studies to determine the development mix and is exploring potential partnerships with strategic investors.
The project will be developed on the company's available landbank adjacent to its existing hospitality assets, Waldorf Astoria Cairo Heliopolis and Hilton Cairo Heliopolis.
The company said it is also studying the construction of a tunnel or bridge connecting the hotels with the new development, although no decision has been announced.

In July, Gulf Egypt had announced the development of a 20 billion Egyptian pound ($384.76 million) integrated hospitality and lifestyle destination in Sharm El Sheikh, according to the company’s website. The development, which will span 354,458 square metres along the Red Sea coast with 750 meters of natural beach frontage, comprises luxury hotel, branded residences, a beach club, wellness and retail elements. The project was structured in coordination with Egypt’s Tourism Development Authority (TDA). Global real estate consultancy JLL conducted market feasibility studies, economic modeling, and master planning, while HVS led hospitality asset evaluations.
URC is the real estate arm of Kuwait Projects Company Holding (KIPCO).
(Writing by Marwa Abo Almajd; Editing by Anoop Menon)
